messages:
anya: quick heads-up: we're proposing an hourly_aggregates table + a small materialized view for the console to avoid heavy joins on raw_events. dual-write from ingest + backfill. RFC link: https://go/rfcs/hourly-aggregates (short summary below)

ben: is this mostly to speed up dashboard reads or to reduce ingest/read costs too?

anya: both. dashboards do many joins + jsonb scans. idea: keep raw_events as source of truth, dual-write into hourly_aggregates (compact) and maintain a route_agg_mv for console reads. reduces p99 and read IO.

mike: dual-write -> reconciliation headache. what's plan for consistency and replays?

anya: steps: 1) dual-write behind feature flag, 2) backfill job reads raw_events to populate hourly_aggregates, 3) expose canary read path (5% routes), 4) monitor diffs and promote progressively.

sophia: which checks during canary? mismatch rate, p99 latency, index read IOPS, and per-route cardinality changes?

anya: yep. add metrics pipeline: 
```
- mismatch_rate = mismatched_rows / sampled_rows
- p99_console_read_ms
- index_read_iops
- per_route_cardinality_delta
```

nate: sampling needs to handle tail routes. propose stratified checks: heavy routes sampled statistically, tail routes use deterministic hourly checksums and any mismatch fails the route.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: flag "hourly_aggregates_dualwrite" -> staging -> canary group alpha (5%)

ben: rolling back partial dual-write sucks. we should make writes idempotent. use idempotency key (route_id, hour, write_version).

mike: upsert on (route_id, hour) with write_version monotonic works. backfill stamps write_version too.

anya: we'll include source_version and last_seen columns to simplify reconciler.

sophia: read fallback — if MV misses a row, do we sync query raw_events? that could spike latency for interactive pages.

anya: fallback policy: try MV, if miss then async-refresh and mark UI as "stale" for that route. only do sync-refetch for quota/billing pages.

nate: retention/backfill window: hot raw_events kept 60d. backfill should finish within that; ops can extend retention per-tenant during backfill if needed.

ben: schema shape? what fields in hourly_aggregates?

anya: sample DDL in RFC: 
```
CREATE TABLE hourly_aggregates (
  route_id TEXT,
  hour TIMESTAMPTZ,
  requests BIGINT,
  errors BIGINT,
  avg_latency_ms DOUBLE PRECISION,
  quota_profile TEXT,
  route_tags JSONB,
  source_version INT,
  canary_verified BOOL DEFAULT false,
  last_seen TIMESTAMPTZ,
  PRIMARY KEY (route_id, hour)
);
```

mike: partition by range(hour) monthly to allow efficient pruning/backfill.

anya: yes. backfill writes into partitions directly; backfill job creates partitions ahead of time.

sophia: console migration: add new datasource + flag to point specific UI cards to hourly_aggregates for canary routes only. how to flip globally?

anya: rollout: 5% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over ~2 weeks with automated verification gates and manual check for quota-affecting pages. billing switch is separate.

nate: alerts: mismatch_rate > 0.1% for big routes, any mismatch for tail routes; p99 regression > 20%; backfill lag > 1h for >5% partitions.

ben: emit diffs to kafka (telemetry-sanity) for replay and debugging?

anya: agreed. send compact diffs (route_id,hour,delta_summary) with 7d retention.

mike: ops runbook: how to re-sync a single route?

anya: backfill CLI: `./backfill --route $ROUTE --start 2026-03-01 --end 2026-03-07` or admin UI force-upsert. runbook includes safety checks and idempotency validation.

sophia: can we mark rows as canary_verified after reconciliation to simplify queries until full promotion?

anya: yes, we'll set canary_verified=true once reconciler validates.

ben: billing consumers must not switch to hourly_aggregates until 100% promotion + 48h verification window. add explicit migration step.

deploy-bot: canary deployment done: flag enabled for canary alpha. monitoring dashboard: https://go/mon/hourly-agg-canary

mike: i'll pair with ops tomorrow for the initial backfill run. thanks everyone. :rocket:
